page.layout: Running head at top: page number 384 left, title "PAVLLI MERVLÆ COSMOGRAPHIÆ" centred; below it the catchline "Campania." centred. Engraved map of Champagne occupies the upper centre (no text transcribed as main text). Below the map one full-width text column with marginal notes in the left margin ("Remi," and "Catalauni,") and right margin (numbers 30, 40, 50 beside the lines).

main_text.p: mæo: Fœderatos idem Plinius indigetat: Civitatem Lingonum habet Notitia Provinciarum in Lugdunensi i. Exstat Cohortis ii. Ling. Eq. memoria in elegante Inscriptione, quæ visitur in Piceno vel Marchia Anconitana, in opido, quod olim Forum Sempronij, vulgo Foßambrone: Hodie La Duché, Pairie & Euesché de Langres. Lingonum sæpe meminit Martialis, obliquè eos subinde perstringens. Occurrunt crebro apud eundem Lana, Saga, Tomenta, & Bardocuculli Lingonum. Remi apud 30 Cæsarem & Plinium, qui Ῥήμοι apud Ptolemæum & Strabonem: Fœderatos Plinius nominat: Civitas Remorum Notitiæ Provinciarum in Lugdunensi ii: Duché, Pairie & Archevesché de Reims. Remorum fines Romanorum tempore latissimi fuere; Sequanis, Mediomatricibus, Treviris, Veromanduis, Suessionibus conregionales. Cæsare Gallias administrante post Heduos secundum Dignitatis locum obtinebant. Nominat ipsorum Senatum idem Cæsar, & civitatis Principem atque Præfectum Vertiscum, de quo in Ephemeridibus Belli Gallici multa. Catalaunos, præeuntibus Membranis; scribendos monent Viri docti, qui in Vulgatis Ammiani Marcellini libris Cathelauni. Sic etiam nominantur in exaratis calamo codicibus Eutropij, qui Tetricum notat ab Aureliano superatum apud Catalaunos. Catalaunorum Civitas; 40 Notitiæ Provinciarum Galliæ in Lugdunensi ii, L'Euesché de Chaalon. Ad hos Catalauni pertinent Campi, in quibus prælio magno superatus ab Romanis, Gothis & Francis, Ducibus Actio Patricio, Theodorico & Merovæo, Hunnorum Rex Attila, anno ab V. C. cıɔ cc iii. Imper. Cæsare Fl. Marciano P. F. Augusto & Clodio Adelphio V. C. Romæ Coss. ab Christo nato cccci, cæsis utrimque clxii millibus, exceptis xc millibus Gepidarum & Francorum, qui paulo ante occubuerant. Legendi Sidonius Apollinar. Carm. vii, Cassiodorus lib. iii Variar. Epist. i & alibi, Paulus Diaconus lib. v, Isiodor. in Chronic. Iornandes de Rebus Goth. cap. xxxvi, & seqq. Gregorius Turonensis variis locis, Aimoinus lib. i, cap. vi, Sigebertus in Chronic. Otto Frisingensis lib. iv, cap. xxvi, Freculphus Lexoviensis lib. 50 v, cap. xiv, Tom. ii, Idacius M. S. Sabellicus Ennead. viii, lib. i, Gaguinus lib. i, & alij. Delineat hos Campos, locumque Pugnæ Iornandes, cap. xxxvi: Convenitur itaque in Campos Catalaunicos, qui & Mauricij nominantur, c. Leugas, ut Galli vocant, in longum tenentes, & lxx in latum: cap. xxxviii; Erat autem positio loci declivi tumore, in modum collis excrescens. Et in fine cap. Fit ergo de loci opportunitate certamen. Attila suos dirigit, qui cacumen montis invaderent, sed à Thorismundo & Aetio præventus est, qui elutiati collis excelsa ut conscenderent, superiores effecti sunt, venientesque Hunnos Montis berri- ficio

page.notes: Left margin notes "Remi," and "Catalauni," are small marginal catchwords beside the lines. The map is an engraving of Champagne (labels such as CHAMPAIGNE, BOURGOGNE/BURGUNDIA, PARIS, Pi. Cardie, Beauce) and is not transcribed. Several words in the small map and the Greek word Ῥήμοι are read with uncertainty; the Roman numeral "cıɔ cc iii" is printed as in the scan.
